findings.title: settings.json template-vs-active registration gap is bidirectional: repo template registers periodic-extract but active does not; active registers auto-build/18 others but repo does not — the repo file IS the template (no separate settings.json.template exists)
findings.observe_how: There is no settings.json.template — `.claude/settings.json` is the only settings file (it is the new-machine template, NOT auto-synced per sync-known-gaps.md). It registers periodic-extract (line 429) but active ~/.claude/settings.json does not; conversely auto-build is in active only via _register-auto-build.cjs. A new machine bootstrapped from the repo template gets periodic-extract but the 18 active-only registrations (incl package-install-guard) are absent.
findings.telemetry: Extends SEED-15 (18 active-only incl package-install-guard supply-chain guard absent from template). NEW: the reverse leak — periodic-extract is template-only and dead in the live machine, and there is no distinct *.template file, so the repo settings.json doubles as both source-of-truth and per-machine config, guaranteeing drift. Reconcile the template against a curated registration manifest.

notes:
Scope: D7a triage of the 35 src_but_never_registered_active hook sources. All 35 read/verified (header comment block + event markers + import-statement grep + git last-touch + presence in repo AND active settings.json).

Method note correcting the prompt's premise: there is NO separate `settings.json.template` in the repo — `.claude/settings.json` is the only settings file and doubles as the new-machine template (it is intentionally NOT auto-synced, per sync-known-gaps.md). All registration claims above were checked against that file and against the active `C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/settings.json`.

Triage distribution of the 35:
- SAFE-DELETE: 1 (test-build).
- DEAD/NEUTRALIZED → delete after deregistration: 1 (auto-build; registered active-only as inert no-op).
- LIB-CODE-MISPLACED & LIVE (exclude from deletion backlog): 4 (daemon-client[11 importers], skill-router, skill-validation-prompt, transcript-parser).
- LIB/ABSTRACTION ORPHAN (investigate→likely delete): 2 (hook-error-pipeline[0 importers], diagnostics CLI[0 importers, manual tool]).
- LATENT-FEATURE, KEEP (dormant, recoverable; telemetry-dead is NOT sufficient to delete): 21, of which the 6-member TLDR-daemon injection hook family (arch-context-inject, edit-context-inject, impact-refactor, post-edit-notify, session-start-dead-code, signature-helper) plus daemon-client lib are the pre-codegraph era.
- LATENT, INTENTIONALLY OFF / DEAD-BY-DESIGN, KEEP: 2 (pageindex-navigator disabled 2026-06-01 per code-intel-boundaries.md; sync-to-repo deliberately unregistered per git-sync-workflow.md, 'Source retained').
- LATENT/SUPERSEDED → investigate before delete: 3 (handoff-index vs session-end-handoff-indexer; session-start-parallel vs session-start-context-loaders/memory-loaders; typescript-preflight vs post-edit-diagnostics).
- TEMPLATE-ONLY registration gap (FIX, keep hook): 1 (periodic-extract — repo-only-vs-active outlier).

Cross-links: D7a-05 extends SEED-15 (settings template gap). The TLDR-daemon hook family being dormant is consistent with the codegraph/code-intel migration documented in code-intel-boundaries.md — pre-codegraph TLDR-injection hooks left in place but unwired.

Deletion-backlog precision: only test-build is unconditionally safe-delete. auto-build is delete-after-deregistration. The 4 LIB modules and the LATENT/intentionally-off hooks must NOT enter the backlog. 5 (hook-error-pipeline, diagnostics, handoff-index, session-start-parallel, typescript-preflight) warrant investigate-then-decide because each has a plausible live supersessor or is an unadopted abstraction — verify the supersessor covers the behavior before removing.
